subject: cloudSheep
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: sheep made of cloud floating.
Style: Kirby.
reasoning:
I'm planning a cute Kirby-style cloud sheep design—round pastel body, shiny eyes, blush cheeks, stubby feet—and thinking through whether it floats above the ground or touches down at y=0.

I'll make the body hover slightly with little round feet dangling to touch y=0, surrounded by small cloud-wisp puffs beneath the belly, with the body center around y≈0.55. For materials, I'm picturing a chubby cloud-puff cluster for the body in soft white-blue shading, topped with a round Kirby-pink face with big expressive eyes and blush marks.

For the finer details, I'm giving the sheep small spiral pale-gold horns, floppy pink ears, coral-pink oval feet, and a cloud-puff tail, plus a scattering of tiny star sparkles floating nearby for a touch of magic. For the rig, I need a skeleton with a spine chain running to neck, head, and jaw, stubby two-joint leg chains with foot tips, ear joints, and a tail chain, plus a separate lower jaw piece shaped as a small flattened pink-red sphere with a tongue for the open mouth.

Now I'm pinning down exact coordinates with the head facing +Z: the body centered around [0,0.62,-0.02] with roughly 0.38 radius, and a larger head centered at [0,0.72,0.36] with 0.24-0.25 radius to keep Kirby-style big-head proportions, topped with a wool puff cap and forelock. I'm placing four short stub legs with hips and shoulders at roughly ±0.2 on x, with oval foot ellipsoids resting near the ground, connected by short two-joint limb chains to the body.

For the floating feel, I'm deciding to keep the legs short and slightly tucked rather than fully dangling, and adding small wispy cloud puffs beneath the belly and trailing off the tail to suggest the cloud-sheep is floating rather than standing. Now I'm starting to define the skeleton hierarchy, beginning with a hips root and a spine chain curving up toward the chest.

Next I'll add the neck chain running from the chest point up to the head base, using two names to produce a span plus a tip joint, then attach a head joint pointed forward off the neck's end, parented to the neck tip.

For the jaw, I'm placing a hinge joint near the head's lower-front area, roughly below and slightly forward of head center, aiming it toward the mouth location, then sketching the lower jaw as a small wedge shape.

I'll keep the jaw closed and draw the mouth as a dark curved decal on the head's underside instead of a separate opening, then add a peach-pink chin ellipsoid below as the jaw, matching the head's face color.

I'll go with jaw opened slightly at 10 degrees so the mouth cavity stays visible rather than hidden by a closed pose.

For the eyes, I'm picturing Kirby's signature tall ovals—dark on top, a bluish gradient below, with a white highlight ellipse and a small lighter spot for depth. I'll texture these as a decal applied to the head sphere, sized small and positioned on either side of the head's front.

For materials, I'll skip the toon kit and write custom shading for the clouds instead—warm white on top fading to a lavender-blue tint below with subtle noise, using the paint, mix, noise, and smoothstep utilities from the core SDK, plus the glow kit for any sparkle effects. I'm confirming which exports are safe to pull from the index versus the kits, then moving on to building the wool-like cloud puffs.

For the puffs, my plan is to scatter low-poly spheres of varied sizes across the chubby base body to create a cumulus-like, overlapping rim, with bigger clusters on top for character and a cloud-fringe around the face—keeping the triangle budget reasonable with roughly 120 puffs at low geometry detail.

I'm shading them with a gradient paint that blends white at the top, soft sky-blue-lavender toward the bottom based on surface normal and position, with a hint of warm blush worked in through noise, skipping outlines to stay true to the soft Kirby-like aesthetic. For the main body, I'm building an ellipsoid shape by lofting over the spine bones, though I'm considering simplifying it to a large scaled sphere parented to the spine2 bone instead.

Deciding between a simple scaled sphere versus a full loft with stations along the body axis for width and height variation, rigged to the hip and spine bone chain. I'm settling on the loft approach with stations tapering from narrow at the ends to widest in the middle, then converting that lofted shape into a surface so I can scatter the puffs across it using the random generator.

Planning the puff layer now: smaller cloud bumps (radius 0.07–0.13) scattered densely across the whole body surface to hide the loft underneath, plus a secondary scatter of larger, sparser puffs (radius ~0.15) to create a lumpier, more defined silhouette along the sides and top.

Now I'm figuring out how the seating/embed math actually works geometrically -- trying to determine whether the part's origin sinks relative to its own bounding box or its center, since that determines how deep each sphere sits into the surface for a given embed value.

I'm settling on roughly 0.5 embed for half-sunk puffs, then thinking through scatter placement rules (rejecting buried points against the body target) and how I'll build the head sphere part with scale, relying on surface decal reading world-space triangles, before moving to pick a soft peach face color.

For the face I'm leaning toward a Kirby-style pink (#ffb7cf) that reads well against white wool, with blush ovals made from radial-gradient pink-red decals and tall oval eye decals. I'm also planning a ring of wool puffs around the back and top of the head to form a hood-like cap using surface placement by elevation and azimuth.

For the puff placement I want to avoid the front face zone so forelock tufts sit cleanly above the eyes, filtering by elevation/azimuth so nothing overlaps brows or eyes. For ears, I'm thinking floppy pink rounded triangles extruded from a leaf-shaped outline, hinged sideways-downward from the head sides with a simple hinge joint per ear.

Working through the cross product confirms thickness is mostly vertical, giving a flat horizontal leaf shape that droops nicely for the ear.

For the ears, I'm placing the root at the side of the head, then layering a smaller inner pink leaf slightly above the main ear outline with a tiny thickness difference for depth. I'm thinking the outer ear could be cream/fluffy colored with a lighter pink interior.

For the horns, I'm planning curly spiral shapes in a pale gold/cream tone, sprouting from the sides of the head above the ears. I'm defining a manual spiral function with turns, radius, and pitch parameters, starting each coil from the hit point on the skull and curling outward.

The coil wraps around the sideways axis, with sign flipped per side to mirror correctly for left/right horns, so turns go as -s*1.15 around axis [s,0,0].

I'm checking whether the horn might collide with the head geometry—estimating the hit point on the head surface at that azimuth/elevation and comparing it against the coil's center offset and radius to see if it stays clear of the skull.

I'll make the pitch larger so the horn spirals outward from the head over about 1.1 turns, starting from a higher elevation point, with a tapered tube radius. For texture, I'm considering adding alternating cream and tan color bands along the sweep to give it a ridged, striped look.

For attaching it, I'm sprouting the horn from the skull surface using the head's geometry origin as the anchor point, with a fallback for null hits. The fluffy head cap should hide the horn's base nicely. Then for the feet, I'm planning coral-pink ovals with slightly darker undersides, connected by short stubby cloud-white legs.

For the leg structure, I'm setting up a chain from hip to knee to ankle, using IK limb targeting so the knee bends forward naturally -- though I need to check the reach distance since the hip-to-foot span may exceed the leg's natural length, which would straighten the joint instead of bending it.

So I'm adjusting the segment lengths to 0.17 and 0.16 for a slight bend that fits the reach. The leg root sits hidden inside the body's puff layer, and I'm thinking about visibility -- only the lower portion from the belly down to the foot is exposed, so I want a small fluff cuff ring near the top of the visible leg to blend it into the body puffs.

I'm placing a ring of six puffs around the ankle joint, oriented outward from the bone axis so they form a cuff where the leg meets the foot, using small embedded spheres at radius 0.07 around the joint.

For the feet, I'll keep them simple ovals with a lighter sole highlight and tiny heel detail, plus countershading with deeper coral underneath. Arms can be skipped since this is a quadruped sheep form, but I should add a cloud-puff cluster tail near the hips.

Writing tail curve logic...

The callback only receives `at`, so I'll size puffs using at.t for a tapering radius along the chain. For underside belly puffs, I think the scatter already covers that region, so I can skip adding extra spheres there and instead focus on a few orbiting sparkle puffs to sell the floating feel.

I'll add 3 small detached mini-cloud clusters rigged to the hips plus 3 glowing star sparkles for a playful Kirby-style accent, keeping it modest—maybe a tiny cloud wisp trailing under the tail and a few floating stars rather than any extra accessories like bows or tags.

For textures, I'm planning around 5-12: an SVG eye, blush, tiny nostril details for the snout, a glowing star texture for the sparkles, and some curly wisp decals for the cloud's fluffy highlights.

Rounding out the texture list to about six: eye, blush, swirl, star, sparkle highlights, plus painted details for cloud, face, horn, foot, and ear. For the mouth, rather than a 3D cavity I'm thinking of a dark decal shape with a tongue and smile corners placed on the jaw geometry, using a half-ellipsoid bowl shape for the lower jaw.

Simplifying further: a flattened dark red ellipsoid for the mouth cavity embedded near the lip line, with the jaw as a separate chin ellipsoid holding a pink tongue sphere, rotated slightly open. I'll decide I don't need a nose since Kirby-style characters skip it, maybe just tiny nostril dots instead.

Positioning the head as a sphere centered around [0,0.76,0.37] with radii [0.26,0.235,0.235], placing eyes symmetrically at x=±0.085, slightly above center, projected onto the front surface as small decals with Kirby-style closed/curved shapes.

For blush and eyes, I'll use the sphere's nearest-point hit function to automatically compute surface position and normal direction, which simplifies placing decals that curve correctly with the head's geometry instead of manually computing projection angles.

Now for the mouth, since eyes are mirrored symmetrically, I just need one calculation that applies to both sides. I'm placing it slightly below the eyes on the lower face, solving for the ellipsoid's z-depth at that y-position so the mouth decal sits properly on the curved surface.

I'm figuring out the mouth cavity position and scale, then setting up the jaw bone with its joint and aim direction, plus a chin ellipsoid and small pink tongue sphere, before rotating the jaw open about twelve degrees so the chin drops down and back.

Checking whether the head sphere's lower surface sits above the chin: computing the head's y-extent at the relevant z slices confirms the chin pokes out slightly below the head surface, so it stays visible, while the cavity and tongue remain tucked just above the chin's top edge.

Adjusting the jaw's scale and center position so the cavity spans roughly 0.636 to 0.70, with the chin centered around 0.612 — that way opening the mouth shifts the chin down and reveals more of the cavity naturally. I'll keep the tongue pink at the cavity's base for contrast.

I think a simpler, more readable Kirby-style small open mouth works better here. For the head geometry, I'll use a smooth sphere rather than faceted, since the face reads better that way. For the cloud hood, I'm scattering puffs across the skull but filtering them to only appear on the back and top.

Now I'm placing the forelock and sideburn puffs — small clusters at specific elevations and azimuths so the hair flanks the cheeks without covering the eyes, which sit around 10° elevation on the head. I'm also starting to lay out the body's spine stations, defining width and height at each z-position along the torso.

I'm sketching the skeletal spine path through hips and spine joints, deciding how the loft should run along that chain and how the bone references should connect the root to the spine tip.

Then I'm calculating body proportions—checking the width-to-height ratios so the body looks appropriately chubby like a sheep while keeping the head proportionally large, Kirby-style. I'm also figuring out where the legs should attach to the belly, computing root positions along the body's curved underside so the leg stubs emerge naturally from the correct x and z coordinates.

Now I'm working out the foot placement for front and back legs—setting ankle targets and foot centers with forward-pointing toes, then defining the limb chain parameters (root, target, segment lengths, and bend directions) so the forelegs bend forward at the knee and the hind legs bend backward at the hock like a real sheep.

Setting up leg chains next, with hip/knee/ankle joints parented to the appropriate spine segment and ground contact points, then sweeping a tapered cloud-colored radius along each leg for the puffy look.

Now I'm attaching the foot as a small ellipsoid bound to the ankle joint, placed and scaled in world-space, and adding a few tiny lighter spheres on the front to suggest toe pads.

Next I'm planning the tail as a chain of points following a smooth curve from the rump, naming segments tail1 through tail3 plus a tip, parented to the hips.

Then I'm adding puffy cloud shapes along the tail path, tapering radius toward the end for a soft cotton look, plus a few floating mini-clouds and stars nearby as extra ambient cues to suggest it's drifting in the sky.

Now I'm defining the cloud paint function, blending shadow and white tones based on surface normal to shade the puffs from top to bottom.

Writing shading and face-paint logic...

Now I'm designing the eye SVG: a dark navy outer ellipse, a blue gradient lower pupil, and a white highlight plus a small secondary light spot, giving that classic Kirby eye look. Next I'll sketch the blush SVG as a simple ellipse shape.

Realizing the cards would get buried if placed directly on the puff-covered body surface, I'm rethinking the approach: instead I should attach the swirl decoration to the puff meshes themselves after they're built, rather than the underlying loft surface.

Checking the part budget: with ~150 puff meshes using shared icosahedron geometry per puff, I'm still well under the 1000-part limit, so merging isn't necessary. I'll use a low-detail icosahedron (detail 1) for each puff, faceted enough to read as cloud-like without being too costly.

Switching smoother spheres would push tris higher, but with ~100 puffs I'm still fine under budget, and I'll keep all puffs using the same cloud color for visual continuity. For the stars, I'm sketching a 5-point star outline alternating between outer and inner radii, then extruding it flat along the z-axis to give it some thickness and a golden glow.

I'll place a few tiny glowing stars floating near the head and tail, bevel them slightly, and add a small rotation to each for variety—skipping extras like bows or necklaces since the wool texture and face are the real standout features.

Now I'm thinking about adding a small cloud-curl forelock on the forehead using a spiral sweep near the top-front of the head, starting with a tuft curling forward from the hit point.

I'm defining the ear joints next, placing earL at the head's surface near the upper-side and angling them outward with a direction vector so they sit naturally against the skull width.

I'm adding an inner ear layer slightly smaller and thicker than the outer ear, colored a lighter pink against the deeper outer pink, then moving on to position the horns relative to the skull using azimuth angles so each side mirrors correctly.

Now I need to make sure the horns clear the ears given their respective elevations, and give the horns a cream-and-gold alternating band pattern. I'm also planning the cloud puffs on the skull cap and checking that the overall model stays within a roughly 1.2m bounding box, sharing one paint sheet across parts with a texel density that accounts for the large painted puff areas.

I'm bumping paint resolution to 2048 to keep the stepped cel-shaded edges crisp, and setting up seeded RNG calls for the scatter placement of puffs, varying their radius by position so they're larger near the top.

For the big silhouette bumps, I'm arranging a ring of larger cumulus-style puffs around the body at varying azimuth and elevation angles, layering them with a finer scatter of 60 smaller puffs on top for texture, while being mindful that the front of the body near the neck/head area may need gaps so the head doesn't get obscured.

I should also add a neck chain to keep the skeleton consistent, running from the spine tip up to the head joint, even though the puffs will visually cover it.

Adding the jaw joint, then working out the ankle ring details with outward-facing spheres, leg side assignment by hip x-position, and glow settings for the gold star sparkles.

Now I'm adding small sparkle accents using crossed card quads with glow applied, counting up the textures used so far (eye, blush, swirl, sparkle), and considering whether to add a wool-curl or cloud-pattern card for extra detail.

I'm skipping a nose feature to keep the Kirby-like simplicity, but weighing whether to add a small gold star decal on the forehead, positioning it based on where the eyes and forelock puffs sit relative to the head's top curve.

I'll aim for a module around 450 lines, favoring quality over sheer length, and now I'm double-checking the builder API details—joint definitions, chain construction, and Catmull-Rom path helpers for the limb curves.

Now I'm working through the body loft, tapering stations to small widths at the ends and confirming that the loft returns a Sweep surface I can pass directly into the surface function. I'm also sketching a small puff helper that sticks sphere geometry onto a frame for cloud-like bumps, and figuring out how to type the frame argument correctly for it.

Writing imports and setup...

Smoothing the shading with blended thresholds instead of hard cutoffs, then layering in pink dapples and a lavender tint near the bottom for softer, more painterly cloud puffs.

For paint colors, I'm applying countershading between lighter and darker hues for the face, feet, and horns. For eye decals, I'm figuring out how the decal placement works against the skull surface — passing a hit point so it can derive both position and surface normal automatically.

I'm computing nearest-surface points on the skull mesh for eye and cheek placement by projecting outward points inward onto the ellipsoid surface.

Now I'm adding a gold star decal near the top of the head, plus mouth cavity, tongue, and jaw coloring, and posing the jaw bone with a slight forward tilt. Then I'm moving on to the spine chain, defining separate bones for spine1, spine2, and spine3 above the hips root.

For the tail, I'm chaining four bones off the hips using a catmull spline through the tail points, then distributing puff spheres evenly along the chain by sampling points at intervals and attaching parts to each.

I'm also adding a glowing star at the tail's tip, generating its outline by computing alternating radii around a rotation point to create the star shape.

Then I'm defining golden star extrusions positioned at the hips, thickened and beveled with a glow effect, and considering how to orient them properly facing forward. I'm sketching out a sparkle card design using a four-pointed star path for a light burst effect.

Then I'm scattering swirl-colored cards across the puff surfaces, giving them random lean and spin so they sit naturally on top with varied orientation, lit like the rest of the surface.

Now I'm working out the body ring bump placements, setting up skin surface sampling and a loop over elevation angles to position bumps around the head and body.

Adding scattered fill puffs for texture, with denser coverage on the underside, bringing the total to roughly 190 puffs across body, head, tail, and cuffs, which keeps the triangle count manageable around 17k if I use a lower-poly sphere segment count.

For the head, I'm scattering smaller puffs filtered to avoid covering the ears and horns while still letting cheek and eye areas show through, then adding explicit puffs for the forelock and sideburns at specific angles so the fluff reads naturally around the face.

Checking the ear placement, I confirm the ear leaf pokes out past the fluff enough to stay visible, attached around y=0.78. For the forelock curl, I'm computing a spiral offset from a point on the skull, positioning its center slightly forward and up so the curl spirals outward correctly.

Checking the sign the other way, rotating negative instead sends the point up and over the top of the head rather than through it, which matches the curl bending backward toward the puffs before coming forward again.

Starting the curl moving forward from the forehead top so it rises and wraps backward works well with radius 0.05, tube tapering [0.032, 0.012], turns around -0.9, flat pitch, hit at elevation 66 az 0. For the horns, I'll reuse similar offset/turn semantics but with center placed down and back from the hit point, scaling turns by the side sign.

Working through the horn rotation math, negative turns about the +x axis mean the curl initially sweeps up and forward then arcs back and down, giving that classic backward-curving ram horn silhouette, with pitch advancing outward along the axis -- so I'll bump radius to 0.085 to match. I'll check that the horn tube doesn't collide with the ear geometry, then set up alternating color bands along the horn length and consider adding small puff details near the horn base.

For the mouth, I'm placing a dark cavity sphere embedded into the head surface, checking that its extent overlaps sensibly with the chin and jaw geometry so a slightly open mouth with a hinge rotation at the jaw looks right once I tilt it down by about 12 degrees.

Now I'm skipping arms and working out limb placement — choosing which spine or hip joint each leg chain should root from, deciding to pass raw points directly into the chain function as a polyline rather than smoothing them, and setting foot center positions relative to each leg's target z-coordinate.

Setting leg radius for a chubby cloud-footed look, then moving into writing the actual build function with helper types and a puff-generation helper for the cloud cuffs.

Writing puff helper function...

Now I'm composing the eye texture SVG with a gradient fill for depth and an ellipse base shape.

Planning sparkle positions and a glow effect for the decal, then setting up the ear's extrude position tied to its joint and bone.

Still writing ear geometry...

Checking that feet, cuffs, and belly puffs all stay positioned correctly relative to the body surface before finalizing the full code.
